definitions.gloss: water tower; elevated water storage tank
definitions.explanation: A tall structure that holds water at height so that it can be supplied to buildings and water pipes by gravity pressure. A standard element of municipal water supply and of large apartment or industrial complexes.

examples.japanese: {高|たか}い{給水塔|きゅうすいとう}。
{丘|おか}の{上|うえ}に{給水塔|きゅうすいとう}が{立|た}っている。
examples.english: A water tower stands on top of the hill.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{団地|だんち}には{必|かなら}ず{給水塔|きゅうすいとう}があった。
examples.english: Older housing complexes always had a water tower.

examples.japanese: {給水塔|きゅうすいとう}は、{高|たか}い{位置|いち}に{水|みず}を{貯|た}めることで、ポンプを{使|つか}わずに{水圧|すいあつ}を{得|え}るための{施設|しせつ}だ。
examples.english: A water tower is a facility that stores water at a high location so that water pressure can be obtained without using pumps.

notes:
Composed of {給水|きゅうすい} (water supply) and {塔|とう} (tower). A tall structure housing an elevated water tank; common in municipal water systems, on factory and apartment-complex roofs, and atop hills.

In Japan, many older {団地|だんち} (public housing complexes) are immediately recognizable by their concrete water towers, which have become a nostalgic architectural motif.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {給水塔|きゅうすいとう}が{建|た}つ: a water tower stands / is built
- {給水塔|きゅうすいとう}に{水|みず}を{貯|た}める: to store water in a water tower
- {団地|だんち}の{給水塔|きゅうすいとう}: the water tower of a housing complex
- {給水塔|きゅうすいとう}を{解体|かいたい}する: to dismantle a water tower

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {給水|きゅうすい}タンク: water tank — a general term; may or may not be elevated
- {貯水|ちょすい}タンク: water storage tank — emphasizes storage function rather than supply
- {貯水池|ちょすいち}: reservoir — a large pool for water storage, typically at ground level
- {配水|はいすい}{池|ち}: distribution reservoir — part of municipal water systems; distributes to individual households
